notes.title: Announcing Release Date
notes.notes: [p]Alone is finally close to release, having been in early access for three years, and a number of milestones later, the game is finally now stable, and featured enough to release it properly.[/p][p]This release also includes some new features - the "Rune" milestone, which includes graphical improvements, the addition of embeddable runes, changes to trade, and much more.[/p][p]The release also sees Alone getting a small tweak to its name.[/p][p]If you're just here for the release date - then here it is :) - [b]October 11th[/b][/p][p]If you're interested in everything else coming out in this milestone, then read on...[/p][p][/p][h1]Name Change[/h1][p]With the upcoming release - the game will be known as [b]Alone: Shattered Tribes.[/b][/p][p]There are multiple reasons for this change. Firstly, when this name was bequeathed, it was a very very different game - there were no tribes to save, it was an unforgiving survival RPG, and you would actually spend the entire game alone. With the updates made to the game since then, this is no longer the case, and the name is no longer accurate.[/p][p]This new name reflects the game itself - where you start off alone, but you must unite the shattered tribes in your new home.[/p][p]You might also notice some changes in the steam page, with a new fancy logo and other similar changes[/p][p][/p][h1]New Trailer[/h1][p]With a new release comes a new trailer, and here it is :)[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="cHdzJrj-RXs;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h1]Graphic Changes[/h1][p]One of the main changes coming with this release is an update to the way the terrain and lighting look. The sharp square tiles are gone, and replaced with something more beautiful looking.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/9a06b0f8d0c7aa87c8fc39a64faa0cd8b21d7f85.png"][/img][/p][p]The lighting has also been adjusted, there's more visibility during night-time, and when exploring dark areas.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/47dac484d2f59ba1b612e0db8a088c75d6c89b00.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/ec25c70c37b08938440c468148cc24ba0105a63d.png"][/img][/p][h1]Runes & Elixirs[/h1][p]The namesake of the update is the Rune system. Runes are rare items which are embedded into weapons to give them great power.[/p][p]Runes can be found randomly as loot, but they can be more reliably obtained by exploring the Crypt.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/96cc6108915cdbb07894e8446f960f04f3fcc882.png"][/img][/p][p]Certain Crypt levels will contain a room like the one shown above. After defeating the enemies guarding it, you can claim one of 7 different types of runes.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/30ed4fdb8ac41f4693a22d5e627197685eec369b.png"][/img][/p][p]Runes are then embedded into weapons at the shrine. [/p][p]Some runes will give a flat bonus of some sort, such as finding nicer loot or gaining faster experience, but other runes need to be charged.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/1682e27ce11a4e4c70ea880146b14a0a4e33e0c2.png"][/img][/p][p]Charging a rune involves defeating enemies, after which you can invoke the power of the rune - a powerful, yet very temporary bonus. Continuing to defeat enemies whilst the rune is active will help recharge it, giving you more time to make use of its powers. Some of the more powerful runes will only trigger when enemies of certain types are defeated.[/p][p][/p][p]Runes come in three levels, with the Mythical runes being the most rare. However, one can Empower runes at the shrine to gain access to more powerful ones, at the sacrifice of 2 other runes which are destroyed in the process.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/f280eac2d2252a66d624760094da76558a68e7d2.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]The intention of this new feature is to allow the player to customise weapons for specific uses. With the more powerful runes restricted to impacting only specific enemy types, having a weapon for each scenario will be the key to maximising benefits.[/p][p][/p][h2]Elixirs[/h2][p]This update also brings with it changes to Elixirs. They are much rarer and more precious now.[/p][p]Additionally, the elixir of healing has been split into three levels:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/8f85c4c8517c9fc33369a5bfc7f8e4b6e89bfb6e.png"][/img][/p][p]Each level will, when drunk, restore your health by a limited amount. At lower levels, the Minor Elixir should be enough, but as you increase in levels, it will no longer heal you fully, and you'll need to make use of the more expensive, and rarer elixirs.[/p][p][/p][h1]Trader Improvements[/h1][p]Trading has been reworked extensively.[/p][p]Previously, trade had some limitations which made it less useful, and quite lacking. Traders were specialised, bringing two classes of items with each visit - for instance, a trader bringing only weapons and armour.[/p][p]This is quite limiting, as not all items are equally desirable. Coupled with the limitation added on the quality of items that are generated, meant that traders which brought weapons or tools would often be ignored, with raw goods traders being far more useful.[/p][p]Moreover, the traders focused primarily on quantity instead of quality. So it would be more likely that a trader brings a large number of cheaper items, instead of a few expensive ones.[/p][p]This milestone changes everything. Now each trader has a certain, fixed, amount of slots. Each slot is restricted to the type of item which it can bring - although some slots are general. This way, the trader is guaranteed to always bring some raw materials and some food with each visit. As the trader becomes richer, they will still bring the same amount of slots, but each item will cost more - meaning higher quality weapons, tools, and armour, and more useful raw materials.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/1e8fc7e15a91f5343c582fb61805f9b90ee41231.png"][/img][/p][p]Additionally, the first slot is guaranteed to be an exotic good. These are goods which can only be obtained through trade - such as fertiliser, or silk. These existed previously, primarily as some late-game building upgrades - but because of the way the items were generated previously, did not show up as often as desired.[/p][p]As part of this milestone, quite a few exotic items have been added - there is now more exotic food, the inclusion of exotic beverages, as well as weapons and armour.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/763492a3cdf4ebe482296a1272eafb382b4632d4.png"][/img][/p][p]Here's a character kitted out with one of the choices of exotic helmet, armour and weapon.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/e7a6f463c7192f919cb6a36a8b294d1e47526621.png"][/img][/p][p]If slots are fixed, then how does one go about getting more items? Through trade upgrades[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/77a49ac1991774f6620210df5b9e1684e33da57f.png"][/img][/p][p]Whilst expensive, you can add up to two additional slots.[/p][p]And these slots are customisable - so you can choose what exactly the trader will bring [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/87f4ad1bc9ab072009ce3ce8f0eb3bd7cafcfc91.png"][/img][/p][p]This can be changed freely whenever a trader is visiting, and will impact any upcoming traders. By planning ahead, you can ensure you will find the specific items you're looking to buy.[/p][p][/p][p]With these changes, the trader should become much more useful, and also grant access to powerful and rare items for those with deep pockets[/p][p][/p][h1]Everpunished[/h1][p]The Everpunished have received some changes as well.[/p][p]Firstly, they now look different, the basic melee Everpunished appearing in three variants making it more clear how dangerous they are. Also they look nicer, just thought I'd mention that.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/a8f28fb783646c4f343c33cc9048cb267ef5193d.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/c470c5482051acec33385619b9baed64544ce4a1.png"][/img][/p][p]In a manner similar to how goblin armies are equipped, as you descend to deeper levels, there are new enemy types which replace the easier ones. For the Everpunished, this includes the crossbow draugr, which replaces the axe thrower.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/931327b0b0223956573b50262c60ac38331ed88e.png"][/img][/p][p]And similar to their goblin counterparts, they will on occasion grant you a temporary penalty if they succeed on a critical hit.[/p][p]They are further joined by the banshee, who's screams strike terror into your heart[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/6f0859ebe3d55eb958dc899220ec222ac4eb8d5d.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1]Forest[/h1][p]The forest has also seen some improvement.[/p][p]Whilst it will remain a place for early, lower level, hunts - if you traverse far enough, you will find something more dangerous.[/p][p]This is one of three types of "boss" enemies.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/87d089a0cbf5d578dd62f129a462c94a2842a458.png"][/img][/p][p]Each of them have their own special attacks, and are formidable enemies in their own right. But defeating them will grant you some unique rewards, so it's worth the risk if you're strong enough.[/p][h1]Wrapping Up[/h1][p]And that's it :) See you on the 11th of October.[/p]

notes.title: Next Milestone Reveal - Rune
notes.notes:
Salutations,

I am pleased to announce some details about the next milestone for Alone. So without further ado...

The next milestone will be called "Rune", and includes a mixture of changes which will impact both the combat, and the living part of the game. As always, it is still in active development, so things are likely to change by the time it is released. Starting with the major features

[h1]First Official Release[/h1]

Alone has been through many many changes since it was first out on Early Access. It has now arrived at a point where I feel it's stable and featured enough to receive an official release.

So what will change after this release? It doesn't mean that the game is entirely and totally done, just that future updates will be more iterative and less gamebreaking than the previous ones.

[h1]Runes[/h1]

Runes are an entirely new feature that will be introduced in this milestone. Runes are items that can be found as loot, and embedded into weapons and will apply powerful bonuses.

Let's start with the motivation behind runes - the idea was to shake things up a bit when it comes to weapon choice. Since all weapons are currently equally powerful against different enemies, there's no real reason to switch or try out different weapons. Once you find a weapon you like, you can use it until it breaks (or you repair it). With runes, it'll be possible to customise weapons to a certain degree, to optimise them for a specific purpose. 

Runes can be obtained just like normal loot - although they are quite rare, especially the more powerful ones.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/51b07d79793bd346c8c9183c35b83f57ae785f61.png[/img]

Runes come in three levels - Faded, Normal, and Mythical - and they can have one of many different effects. Some effects involve increasing the loot that you'll find, how quickly you gain experience - whilst others will occasionally grant powerful temporary bonuses to help you in combat. These bonuses are always limited to triggering when you fight enemies of a specific faction - this way, the weapon which is most suited to fighting the undead might not necessarily be the best weapon for fighting goblins - if one has a specific rune embedded into it.

Embedding runes happens at the shrine. A weapon can only have 1 rune embedded into it - and trying to embed another one will replace the previous one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/c255f5b06063030b45f07fb08f7a5c6236fd8036.png[/img]

Once the rune is embedded, it'll show on the interface as part of the weapon details.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/5f0355a25af015836b031c84503ded6cd10e9fb1.png[/img]

Runes can also be empowered at the shrine. Finding a Mythical rune is very rare indeed, but you can make one yourself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/845a364055106fd041b4fbaba2b2a0a14ce53bdc.png[/img]

Empowering a rune requires 3 runes of the same level - but not necessarily of the same type.  Two of the runes will be destroyed, and the primary rune will be empowered by a level.

[h1]Trade Changes[/h1]

Another major change is handling how trade works. 

Starting with the motivation again. The trader is currently not as useful as they can be. Currently, each trader is specialised, and will primarily bring items of two types - but this is rather limiting. For a start, not all items are equally desirable - and certain items - weapons, armour, and tools - are only going to be useful if they are of high quality, which the trader rarely brings because of their price - preferring to bring many cheaper items instead of a few expensive ones.

This will change in the next milestone. The trader now has a fixed amount of "slots", with each slot being of a specific type (although some slots are general). As a trader gains more money, the value of each slot will increase - meaning they will bring nicer items, including tools, weapons, and armour of a quality that should be acceptable. One of the slots is always going to be for food, and another for raw materials - meaning that the trader should always bring something worth purchasing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/22cf2926af4f5e1da80a4a513d136dccdfe7dbf4.png[/img]

And the first slot is always guaranteed to be an exotic good. These are goods which can only be found from the trader. They did exist previously, but now they are going to be more accessible. 

Also as part of this milestone, quite a few new exotic items have been added, including foods, drinks, as well as weapons and armour.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/90197e107be9271d1af1210955765b6272bad3d4.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/68a58d14a081a106085a76f3dd26415901de5e95.png[/img]

Also, the trade post has received two new upgrade paths - which unlock two additional slots. What do these slots bring? It's up to you...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/26e2230dc874c707897001a6b645b9b3ef50eb22.png[/img]

Through the new Agreements tab - the player can choose what sort of items they want the trader to bring in these additional slots. The first unlocked slot even allows the bringing of more exotic items.

[h1]Everpunished and Forest[/h1]

The Everpunished have also received some updates. Firstly, they now look a little different - making it more clear which are the more dangerous of the lot.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/cb42ce54b0087b7d31840164076c274171c678da.png[/img]

Similar to goblins, there are now also some more special undead at higher (or should that be lower) levels. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/f192e625e95d6eaf79d7370ceb42e583af2b1c17.png[/img]

And similar to the goblins, they will occasionally land a critical hit on you and apply some nasty effects. At higher levels, the axe-throwers will be replaced by crossbows, and the banshee will make an appearance, who's powerful screams can leave you stunned.

The undead aren't the only ones who will receive an update in the next Milestone. The forest has been changed as well.

The forest will continue to remain the easiest area to hunt in, a good place for newer characters to earn some skill, and collect much needed resources - but for those who want to advance further - it'll get a bit more dangerous.

Now the forest will contain one of three "boss" enemies. When defeated, they will grant access to some fancy loot - but they are very dangerous - and their special abilities make them even more so.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/60f82a874f4ce6df12a6d2ab4835c666064363ac.png[/img]

[h1]Smaller Changes[/h1]

There will be other smaller changes and improvements included, as always. One of the changes comes as a suggestion of bicZoid - having the name of the item and not just icons - and should help readability when determining which resources are needed for an upgrade or a building.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/3ffb4f7ca0e267201b9b5443b6e96844bfce328d.png[/img]

So, what do you think ? Is there anything that particularly has you excited ? Do you have any suggestions or any improvements to recommend? I would love to hear them.

notes.title: Tribe (0.13) Released
notes.notes:
The Tribe Update drastically changes the late to end game. It replaces the blighted island concept and replaces it with a number of missions.

Below is a summary of the changes that you will find in this release

[h1] Major Features [/h1]
[list]
[*] Story - Our hero's story has been fleshed out and the driving force behind their actions is made more clear
[*] Cutscenes - This release ntroduces two sets of cutscenes as a prequel to our hero's adventure - and as an explanation of the impact their adventure has had on the islands
[*] Missions - The removal of the blighted island concept, and it's replacement with 7 new missions - each offering different challenges, some spread over multiple maps.
[*] Blood Brothers - Completing missions gives you access to Blood Brothers, which can be assigned to gather resources or help with crafting
[*] Companion - The ability to set a Blood Brother as a companion, who will offer you support in combat
[*] Tribehome & Services - Completing missions builds up the Tribehome. This can offer certain services such as item repair or training at higher levels.
[/list]

[h1] Minor Features [/h1]
[list]
[*] New Goblins - The introduction of new specialised goblin types to hinder the player at higher levels
[*] New Bosses & Special Enemies - The introduction of new bosses and special enemies for certain missions
[*] Enemy Crits - Some higher level enemies can land critical hits, which will cause a debuff on the player for a while
[*] New Achievements - New achievements have been added (including 1 hidden one) to reward the player for succeeding in their quests
[*] Conversations - Some friendly villagers can be talked to for information about the world, or the missions ahead
[*] Graphic Updates - New splash screens and new start menu
[/list]

Please note that as this is a major change - save games from the previous releases are not compatible.

I hope you enjoy the latest update, and look forward to any feedback

notes.title: Tribe Update Releasing Soon
notes.notes:
The Tribe Update drastically changes the late to end game. It replaces the blighted island concept and replaces it with a number of missions.

And it will be released soon - specifically on the [b]7th of December[/b]

Let's take a look at what to expect with this next release

[h1]New Trailer[/h1]
With the large changes that this release will bring, it is only fitting that the trailer changes to reflect it.

[previewyoutube=nFlNPS5TGZ4;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]The Story[/h1]
This release introduces and fleshes out our hero's story. Their village having been razed by goblins and their companions taken captive, they escape, only to shipwreck on the island.

Our hero's story is now shown in a number of cutscenes which play before gameplay starts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/f5864e8453efbd2677a2feab45900b4b22de46dd.png[/img]

And after having survived and settled on the island, our hero will work to unite the other tribes being menaced by the goblin foe, and hoping to finally rescue their companions.

A scene from their escape is also displayed in the main menu, and used for character customisation

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/e0fc6fa3b45aee956adb035044c5c71dcb3def0b.png[/img]

[h1]Missions[/h1]
The blighted lands concept has been changed and replaced by a number of missions.

After our hero repairs the ship, they can visit each island in turn, with each island containing a different mission.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/da81e70e299702aeaf5fa29f032228b6003ddf9f.png[/img]

With each mission, our hero finds a tribe which is in trouble, or takes the fight to the goblins. Each mission is entirely different, and whilst some of them do have procedurally generated maps, the rest have custom made maps and custom code to support them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/51f719e266ef7dff108122b2a5c4f35210e7e0f5.png[/img]

Most of the missions include some degree of combat, but with certain missions, the more economic focused hero can use their resources to make things easier.

For instance - this mission involves defending a fortress from waves of goblin attackers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/e3878f135a7cffb22584db38c9545c54bc43dec6.png[/img]

If we want to make the fight easier - we can purchase some mission specific upgrades - such as the healing supplies upgrade which allows you more healing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/57af0971de9bd7a91b6b0e1189d655847e798624.png[/img]

This should allow players who prefer to focus on the economic side of the game, to made combat just that bit easier.

[h1]Blood Brothers[/h1]
In previous versions of the game, blighted islands could be claimed and specific buildings could be placed to grant our hero some extra resources. This feature has been replaced by the concept of a Blood Brother. When completing each mission, the player will unlock at least one blood brother (some missions grant more than one).

By using the desk, the player can assign blood brothers to specific tasks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/dab5f9f8980970a5465162e4592c2b3e8cbb1833.png[/img]

Depending on the task assigned, every day, our hero may find additional resources in their stockpile. Alternatively they can be assigned to a crafting building to give a bonus to the quality of the items produced. A third option is to assign a blood brother as a companion - this character will join you in the dangerous areas, and fight off enemies with their bow.

[h1]Tribehome & Services[/h1]
A representation of the tribes that our hero is uniting can be found in the Tribehome. This location can be visited from the main island, and gradually expands as our hero completes more missions. With each expansion, the amount of villagers wandering increases, and so do the buildings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/f5f8016becb909f45d1e1dc3c4a422879b3f61ca.png[/img]

Aside from being an interesting location to visit and watch grow, the tribehome also introduces a number of services. Some of the services are limited by the size of the tribehome.

One of the services on offer is the ability to repair one's weapons and tools. If our hero happens to be flush with a lot of money, they can also make use of the combat training on offer at the barracks - although this is expensive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/7a235e54815c15cca6c91252a6da582dc4eeaf74.png[/img]

[h1]New Enemies[/h1]
A new major update wouldn't be the same without some new enemies to fight. Aside from some special boss enemies, the goblins have also received some reinforcements, some of which have special abilities to make them more effective.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/c8dcb1976cca0f111a66249fdf5cc4fa75ca30f8.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/a2aa589837874a6a36f80805a80821f24e0d30da.png[/img]

The rogue and the alchemist are just two of them. The rogue is able to land critical hits - and in so doing, applies a debuff which makes it easier for their friends to harm you.

The alchemist is able to occasionally throw bottles of toxic gas, which will make you weaker if you breathe in too much of them.

[h1]Wrapping it Up[/h1]
There are many other smaller changes which I haven't mentioned here. I hope these changes will make the late to end game more fun.

notes.title: Feature Focus - Missions - Storming the Fort
notes.notes:
In this feature focus we'll take a close look at one of the Missions coming in the next release of Alone. This specific mission is particularly interesting because it can be resolved not only through combat, but players who have focused on the economic aspect can make use of that to make the mission much easier.

To start, here's a video showcasing some parts of the mission. But we'll go through it in more detail either way. As always, development is still in progress, so nothing is finalised and balance changes might be made.

[previewyoutube=onY4e7qvb_c;full][/previewyoutube]

This particular mission is spread over 4 stages and includes 5 maps - so it makes sense to go through them in that specific order.

[h1]Stage 1 - The Siege Camp[/h1]

The player character uses the repaired ship to access the start of this mission. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/467d4e6ec00ed4f34eacdc74b0ced75d124e573e.png[/img]

Each of the islands contains a different mission - this particular one is towards the late mid-game, so the player character is expected to be of a sufficiently high level at that time.

Landing on this island, the player enters a friendly siege camp, which is investing a fortress built by a precursor civilisation, and currently held by goblins. They are preparing to assault it, and are awaiting the player character's direction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/de1d4402c5c69b76c5dbb113919b706d1d4efa79.png[/img]

Entering the camp, the player can talk to the Captain there, to get an idea of the present situation, and use the planning table to purchase Mission Upgrades.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/6e9c2477aff289791ba84f72a0da2f5ceddd3110.png[/img]

Mission Upgrades are bonuses that the player can purchase to help make the mission easier for them. Depending on the type of bonus, these will either cost coins or specific resources. The aim is to allow players who prefer to focus on the economic aspect of the game to make the combat easier. It is entirely possible to get through the mission without buying a single upgrade, but then it'll be much harder.

Of particular note is the first row of Upgrades - which determine what the first stage will look like - whether to use a battering ram to break down the gate, a siege tower to fight on the walls, or using a Secret Passage to bypass the walls entirely.

This choice determines what the first map will look like. Choosing the Secret Passage will bypass the first stage entirely.

It is important to note that if the player is defeated at any point, the mission fails entirely and they must start over - although upgrades will persist between attempts.

[h1]Stage 2 - Battering down the Gate[/h1]

This is the default map for the first stage, and the hardest option. In this part of the mission, the player has to guard a battering ram whilst it slowly moves up towards the gate.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/bc20371af9ead60aba2dd1d32a94d359f1ea446f.png[/img]

You'll notice a blue circle around the ram. If any enemies are present in that circle, the ram will stop moving until they are defeated - and then it'll continue moving. To keep the mission simple for the player, there's no risk of the goblins destroying the ram, it'll continue to wait there until the enemies are defeated, and the only way to fail this mission is for the player to lose all their health.

Enemies will spawn in a trickle from the two towers and the goblin pit.

If the player keeps the ram safe for long enough, it'll eventually reach the gates and start striking at it. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/d20d45cf1e9bd23cb738450ead2850095f07db26.png[/img]

A short while after, the gates will be destroyed and this part of the mission will be over, leading to Stage 2.

[h1]Stage 2 - Fight on the Walls[/h1]

If the player has paid the appropriate resources to afford a Siege Tower - then the first map will be a fight on the walls. This map is much easier than the Battering Ram map, as the amount of enemies spawned is fixed, and there's enough space to catch your breath between fights.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/42e060793af5fa0e4d8d94a19169e70bbe421acd.png[/img]

Starting at the top of the siege tower, the player must fight on the walls until they reach the gate controls.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/790941306b4eac7a5349e6c057ff0e6403df9a1a.png[/img]

Defeating the enemies defending the controls, pulling the lever to open the gates and let allies inside, and then making their escape through the trapdoor - this stage of the mission will end.

It's a rather straightforward part of the mission - the only exception being the sentries patrolling the walls which will summon more enemies from the nearby towers if they spot you.

But with that all done, the player now advances to the next stage of the mission - the Courtyard.

[h1]Stage 3 - The Courtyard[/h1]

Having successfully broken through the walls, the player now needs to reach the keep. But the goblins have different plans, and have built a crude barricade to block the keep off.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/f04b950a1885b63ba0068003febc0669ce4164df.png[/img]

In this part of the mission, the player must strike a balance between defeating enemies, and destroying the barricade.

The barricade is gradually destroyed by moving the character next to it, and beginning to hammer at it.

However, in the nearby towers, goblins are spawned constantly, and unlike in the Battering Ram map, they will wait until they assemble in large enough numbers before advancing to defend the barricade. If the player neglects the amassing goblins, they might become strong enough to overwhelm them - like the below screenshot shows.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/f55c272a79c3e7dc4ad8624ba6a24a1654e4ae74.png[/img]

This stage has a couple of interesting mission upgrades specific to it. One of the upgrades destroys one of the spawning towers, making the fight much easier. Another of the upgrades increases the speed at which the player destroys the barricade.

The third upgrade involves the capture of a nearby tower, which will occasionally shoot arrows to damage your goblin foes.

With the barricade broken, the player advances into the last stage - the throne room.

[h1]Stage 4 - The Throne Room [/h1]

This last stage is a boss fight. Having successfully fought their way to the leader of this particular tribe of goblins, the player comes face to face with a large orc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/5075ca18f7a63700592dca721b08afdc68c049c0.png[/img]

Aside from being a dangerous opponent in his own right, the orc also has a couple of nasty tricks up his sleeve. When his health drops below a specific amount, he returns to his throne, and summons some underlings to help deal with you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/ac0abcf2e230f9ea8ecab65e0c921edc1ad58520.png[/img]

Additionally, one of his minions is dragging a treasure chest containing a health potion. If this goblin makes his way to the boss, the boss will drink it and restore some of his health.

And once this boss is defeated, the rest of the goblins flee, the fortress falls, and your Tribehome gets larger.

And that about covers this specific mission.

As a reminder, if you want a more detailed look at the development process, there's a weekly dev diary [url=devdiaries.alone.epicllama.games]available here[/url]

notes.title: Next Milestone Reveal - Tribe
notes.notes:
Been hard at work on the next milestone of Alone - called Tribe. It's time to take a look at some of the major features that will be coming with that release.

[h1]Summary[/h1]
As always, this is all subject to change, and any screenshots are a work in progress. 

The main focus on this milestone is the inclusion of other tribes you can help, liberate, and work with, and in return they will help on your quest to free your people.

The following  main features will be added in this milestone:

[list]
[*] The player character has a story
[*] Perform missions to Unite the Tribes 
[*] Recruit Blood Brothers to help around the island - or in combat
[*] Visit the Tribehome to see how your efforts are progressing
[/list]

[h1]Motivation[/h1]
The primary motivation for this milestone is to make the mid and late game more interesting. Currently, repairing the ship unlocks access to a number of islands, but what you can do on those islands is severely limited.

Whilst there are 2 special islands (and 2 boss battles), the rest of the islands follow the same pattern - defeat goblins, and clear the blighted towers, defeat a small boss, and the island is yours.

Additionally, whilst you can put buildings on the island to get you access to free resources, the amount of resources is limited, and returning to the island every time to add another building is a lot of effort for very little reward.

[h1] In more Detail [/h1]
[h2]The Story[/h2]
The Player Character's story is more defined now, and with that a change in motivation. The Player belonged to a Tribe which was attacked by goblins, and enslaved.  Having escaped during the raid, they find themselves shipwrecked on the island, and after the initial needs of survival and rebuilding are taken care of, the focus shifts on saving their tribe.

However, theirs is not the only tribe that has come under attack from goblin raids, and there are other tribes shattered across the archipelago - which the player will attempt to unite.

[h2]Uniting the Tribes[/h2]
So how does one unite the tribes?

After repairing the ship, the player character gains access to the islands that surrounds them, but instead of each island having Blighted Towers which they will need to cleanse, there is something different on each island.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/47ba09aa4bb71a24c0bd437013ba85ec7f27aa93.png[/img]

Each of these "missions" will be different, but all will result in yet another tribe coming under your banner.

The missions themselves will be hand-crafted, but the maps will still be procedurally generated - and so will change with each playthrough.

The missions aren't all necessarily going to involve combat - some will be entirely peaceful - and some will require a mixture of both economy and might to overcome.

By way of example, let's take a more detailed look at Mission 1. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/322a066f97929bec42a768567b7a2e7e81915438.png[/img]

This is the first mission the player will unlock and it serves as a gentle introduction to the system - with an entirely peaceful mission.

The Player visits a small rocky island which has the remains of a small tribe which are struggling to survive after also fleeing from a goblin raid.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/6ad512f2ab680ee99e7a251ed182b15a10a6857c.png[/img]

By talking to the Village Elder, the player can discuss their predicament and offer to allow them to settle on their island - but to allow them to do so, the player must give them certain supplies to help them make the journey across. Doing so earns the friendship of the tribe.

This is just one example of a type of mission that will be available - others might include raids to free slaves, or the assassination of a Goblin Leader.

[h2]Blood Brothers[/h2]

Instead of claiming the islands and putting buildings on them to gain resources, each tribe that joins unlocks a Blood Brother which you can then assign to help out. You can freely reassign Blood Brothers at any time, although the changes only take effect the very next day.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/95fc1e49b6532bab0a0bc77fa6f6b74d0ad539e2.png[/img]

There are three things you can do with them.

You can either assign them to collect resources of a specific type. This will give you free resources overnight, similar to the current implementation. As you unlock better metals and wood types, the resources they collect will also change. 

You'll be able to purchase upgrades to increase the yields you get, or you can assign more Blood Brothers to the same task.

Alternatively, you can assign them to help out with a specific crafting task. The Blood Brother will appear next to the crafting workshop, and help out with any odd tasks that need doing. In practice this is an increase to the quality or speed (as appropriate) of the items produced, in a similar way to tool upgrades.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/8f2849700b21f13c21f5d531b2ebea1177e7692e.png[/img]

The third task is companionship, and this is when the Blood Brother joins the player character in combat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/f70795318205dd59b149227734d41d10af697267.png[/img]

A couple of things to note on this assignment.

The Blood Brother always uses a ranged weapon, is always out of harm's way, and enemies will entirely ignore them. They will help the player character by loosing their bow at any enemies which are attacking. How skilled they are scales with the player character level, but there will be upgrades available to help them deal more damage.

In short, the Blood Brother system serves as the tangible reward for unifying the tribe, replacing the current system of Outpost buildings for something more flexible.

[h2]Tribehome[/h2]
The Tribehome is where the united Tribes live. It is a separate map which the player can visit using the crossroads, and represents a small village which slowly builds up as more Tribes join the player character.

Like many other things, the map and the building placement is procedurally generated, and the amount of buildings and wandering tribespeople will expand over time. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/e20a7ff9d1f2053282d2fb00baa627ac2501068a.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/4fca24e6995436992b0e96632ddfc57de34c6020.png[/img]

The player character can wander around when they visit, and there will be special villagers they can talk to which might be able to offer certain services once the village is large enough.

Unlike your own part of the island, this village grows on it's own, and you don't have any control over the buildings or their position.

So that's about it. As mentioned always, everything is subject to change. You can follow development week by week here [url=https://devdiaries.alone.epicllama.games/]Alone Weekly Dev Diaries[/url]

notes.title: Alone | Domus Update Released
notes.notes:
It is my pleasure to announce the release of the next major update for Alone - Domus.

The focus of this update is the peaceful part of the game - with changes to building, decorating, and even clothing.

[h1]Major Changes[/h1]

[h2]Building upgrades and changes[/h2]

The buildings available have been changed, with buildings now broken down based on industry instead of raw material. For instance, the new Weaponcrafter building is used to create weapons, shields, and armour - instead of the mason workshop (stone weapons), smithy (metal weapons), carpenter (shields).

Similarly, tools are now all made at the Toolmaker, which is also the source of a great deal of building upgrades.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/efe200bc20dfa8b9e4f5ea3b6f87f0757a8af594.png[/img]

Most buildings are now created in a "basic" state, and must be upgraded to reach their full potential. The type of upgrades available depend on the building type, but for instance, crafter buildings can be upgraded to unlock new materials and give quality bonuses to items created there.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/f5db5350c17a340e1a5f1876c16941135d57d701.png[/img]

[h2]Building Decorations[/h2]

Buildings can now be decorated using a simplified interface. Some items will even allow you to choose their primary colour, helping you keep to a specific palette. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/ee0e55ddf9c3dffa6310dd23080c0502bc104a09.png[/img]

Many more items have been added for decorative purposes, including two new classes of decorative items - carpets and wall decorations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/4c5e061cfe9142421f5b15290a29a092adfa8b34.png[/img]

[h2]Clothing[/h2]

The player character can now change clothing using the new wardrobe item at the house. Clothing however must be unlocked at the tailor workshop. The fancier the clothing, the fancier the material used to create it, including the need for silk - which is not found on your island...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/4494cb936d6ff57959b751c49d1374569db85ec0.png[/img]

[h2]Storage[/h2]

Island storage has been greatly simplified. Instead of having separate chests with their own inventory, now all chests open the same inventory - making it much easier to remember where you left that... thing.

To help with the larger inventory sizes, the interface has been updated to allow for pagination and filtering.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/c635c2a96c105f8bcf2072771633b0305001d1da.png[/img]

[h2]Trading[/h2]

Trading has been given a significant boost in importance. Some of the more exotic items can only be accessed via trade. To help one's trading efforts, trading is now performed at the Trade Post - which can be upgraded to increase trader frequency, and even increase the amount of profit the player makes during a trade.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/88ca92faeb3ea874dd3ea2f000b1dd4513fa38c3.png[/img]

Additionally, trade goods have been introduced. These are items that can be crafted at the appropriate building, and have a higher value compared to others - perfect for squeezing out that extra gold.

[h2]And the rest...[/h2]

There are other changes not mentioned here, so give the game a try and see for yourself. Try out the new decoration features and see what you can come up with.

notes.title: Feature Focus - Clothing & Inventory
notes.notes:
With the next milestone coming soon (an announcement is closer than you'd think) - it's a good time to take an in-depth view at some of the changes coming.

In this feature focus - clothing and inventory.

Clothing in Alone has been a purely functional consideration. You start off wearing civilian clothing, and then as you make armour and helmets, the character dresses up in them. Since this milestone is focused on the peaceful portion of the game, it was time to change it.

For a start, you no longer start dressed in fine garments, but something a little more suited to a castaway

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/5367473230122e07d02100774a77dd55b316150a.png[/img]

Unlike previously, equipping armour won't change your clothing - you now have two sets of clothing as it were - clothes you wear for combat, and clothes that you wear when safe on your home or claimed islands.

In order to change your home clothing, you'll need to use a wardrobe, which is included in the house building. Using this item opens a simple interface to let you change your hat, pants, cloak, and shirt.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/6103b7351f0644ebc38eaed5ebfbebb8230dd81c.png[/img]

By default you have a small choice of pants and shirts, but the rest must be unlocked. And that's where the tailor comes in.

Clothing has been subdivided into 4 levels, and two types (clothing and accessories) - you don't need to create every single piece of clothing individually. By making and using a specific clothing set, you unlock more options at the wardrobe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/97673b4896fbc9440d48a26854f885b134a0b58e.png[/img]

Similar to armour and weapons, the more exotic clothing requires more exotic materials to make. Of particular interest is the Noble Tier of items which uses Silk - which is a good only accessible from traders

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/f83661d04f19e8f985971873cdaa5c479ea34d90.png[/img]

With quite a few items to choose from, it'll be interesting to figure out what suits your character best...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/4494cb936d6ff57959b751c49d1374569db85ec0.png[/img]

So, let's talk about something a little less colourful but just as useful - inventory.

Previously most buildings came with a chest which you could store items in. The chest had a limited but relatively generous capacity, and normally you'd try to store the appropriate items in the appropriate building - say putting all the stone in the mason's workshop.

But since it's a bit annoying to try to remember where everything is, and since the limited capacity wasn't fun either - the whole system has been changed in this milestone. Now all the chests on the island are linked to one central storage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/c635c2a96c105f8bcf2072771633b0305001d1da.png[/img]

So you could, for instance, put wood into the chest in your house, and then take it out in the chest at the carpenter's. It's also of unlimited size - there are page controls at the bottom to allow you to scroll through all the contents.

But since having a lot of items might make it unwieldy, it also comes with filter tabs. Clicking on that tab will filter only items of a specific type, to help you find exactly what you're looking for.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/312cd3e83d5f8300bcd2e4b94b7e92c5535889e7.png[/img]

There are some exceptions to this system. Each island has it's own storage - so you can't teleport items across islands this way. The ship hold is it's own storage however, so you can use that to ferry items across like previously.

Hopefully this system will remove some of the annoyances of looking for a specific item.

And that's it for this Feature Focus. The milestone is very nearly done and an announcement for the release date will be going out soon...

notes.title: Domus Feature Focus - Building Customisation
notes.notes:
With the next release coming soon - it's a good time to take an in-depth view at some of the new features coming.

In this Feature Focus - how you can customise your buildings.

The ability to add and move items around has been a feature in Alone for a while, however the interface was overcomplicated, and there wasn't much choice in items to decorate one's buildings with.

In the upcoming milestone release "Domus" - decorating one's buildings is easier than ever, and includes a lot of items you can craft, loot, or even trade for.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/50832e9ac5bf9a7f93e43bde6e6874fb2ddcdad0.png[/img]

Starting with the changes to the interface. Customisation mode is accessed by using the signpost, as previously, but the interface is much easier to use now - with the items the player has in their inventory shown as large icons.

Adding an item is as simple as clicking on it, and then using the mouse to position it into whichever part of the building it should go

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/9e1b861fd704951e8e769d3ef6e6153977261275.png[/img]

Similarly, if you change your mind about the location of an item, you can simply click on it and move, rotate, or remove it.

Some items come in multiple colours. You don't need to decide on the colour when crafting them, instead you can choose the colour when you position them - and can easily pick again if you change your mind.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/ee0e55ddf9c3dffa6310dd23080c0502bc104a09.png[/img]

Previously you could only position items on the ground, but in the next release, you can decorate your walls with banners, shelves, or decorative weapons. And if you don't like the barren wooden floor, you can make use of the choice of carpets.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/20d6855f60659d8cc689f5d99f28da9c9eb9e1dd.png[/img]

So where do you get such items from? The carpenter and tailor are the two obvious choices - with the carpenter handling the majority of the floor and wall decorations, and the tailor handling carpets and banners. However there are some rare and exotic decorations which can only be obtained as trophies in combat, or from trade - so keep an eye out for those.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/9f776c88085074f8952e82ead175abb35f5e96e3.png[/img]

And to finish things off, here are a few screenshot examples of a house being decorated

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/4c5e061cfe9142421f5b15290a29a092adfa8b34.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/581739712f322322308935370a7d91fcccdbba95.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/495cfdaf4098f69453d1c037bcb14306b794eae7.png[/img]

I'm sure you'll be able to do much better, and curious to see what you all can come up with.

So that's all you need to know about customising buildings. Next time we'll talk about a different type of customisation - clothing.

notes.title: Domus Feature Focus - Upgrades
notes.notes:
With the next release coming in a few weeks' time - it's a good time to take a more in-depth look at some of the features that are going to be implemented. 

Building upgrades are a new feature that will be introduced in the upcoming release. Most buildings can be upgraded, with each building supporting multiple upgrade paths - so it's not a simple case of a "Level 1 XXX".

Each upgrade improves the building in some way - and the best way to explain how this works, is to take a couple of examples - the Trade Post, and the Toolmaker.

[h1]The Trade Post[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/88ca92faeb3ea874dd3ea2f000b1dd4513fa38c3.png[/img]

The Trade post is a new building and is where you'll meet traders when they come visit the island. The basic building looks rather bare - although it can be decorated - more on that in the future, however it has two upgrade paths which can be availed of.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/34904b7203c9b6e56a0364443a7da830facdf07b.png[/img]

The "Trader Comfort" upgrade path gives a bonus to the prices you buy or sell goods at, and that makes them a very useful set of upgrades for those doing a lot of trading. 

The "Access" upgrade path increases the frequency traders arrive at. Trade is going to be much more important - some items can only be accessed through trading - so this is something worth considering.

Upgrades sometimes add new items or modify the building in some way - so here's what a fully upgraded Trading Post looks like.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/3cef03330c002dd0e9db403937d3fdc5e4cac682.png[/img]

[h1]Toolmaker[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/cc06970f81905da8f5ad47213500591420b5d1bb.png[/img]

The Toolmaker is another new building coming with the next release. The toolmaker is where you make all your tools - both stone and metal ones. This includes the hand-tools used for mining, lumberjacking and the like, but it also includes tools used to upgrade other buildings.

If we take a look at the upgrades related to the toolmaker, we find there's quite a lot to go through.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/f5db5350c17a340e1a5f1876c16941135d57d701.png[/img]

Many of the crafter buildings have similar upgrade paths. The four upgrade paths to the left - Stone, Copper, Iron, and Orium all work in very similar ways. Taking the Stone one as an example, each level requires you to have a specific tool in your inventory - made at the Toolmaker's - and once that is consumed and the building upgraded - will give you a bonus to quality, and speed of any stone goods created at this building. Apart from increasing one's Inspiration stat - this is the way to get the nicest and best quality items in the game.

The Copper upgrade path is a little bit different, with the Anvil being the first upgrade - that will unlock an anvil and allow you to create metal tools - you're restricted to making stone ones til then. The rest of the path, and the Iron and Orium ones work exactly like the Stone one.

Taking a look at the Furnace Upgrade path - the first upgrade adds a Smelter - allowing you to make ingots from raw materials. The other two upgrades will reduce the amount of raw material needed to make ingots - very useful especially since coal and ores are quite precious.

And similar to the Trade Post - upgrades make some slight tweaks to the building itself - with the Anvil upgrade unlocking an anvil at the work table, and the Furnace upgrades adding the smelter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/efe200bc20dfa8b9e4f5ea3b6f87f0757a8af594.png[/img]

So that's all you need to know about building upgrades. In the next Feature Focus we'll take a closer look at how you can decorate your buildings and make them look unique.

notes.title: Next Milestone Reveal - Domus
notes.notes:
With Ironwood being released a few weeks ago, it's time to take a look at what's next. And what's next is a milestone called Domus.

[h1]Summary[/h1]
Bearing in mind that everything is subject to change, here's a high level list of what's planned next.

[list]
[*] Buildings can be upgraded
[*] More items available to decorate buildings with, and interface improvements
[*] Change to buildings available, addition of new buildings
[*] More importance given to Trade - Trade goods and items that are only available from trade
[*] Clothing for the player
[/list]
[h1]Motivation[/h1]
One of the primary things that I believe need improvement in Alone, is how the game-loop is combat-centric, and that's really not what the game's focus is. The main rewards on offer for hard work and success are being able to fight stronger enemies, and unlocking better materials to be able to fight stronger enemies. The next milestone is going to be focused more on making your island better, and giving you something else to aim towards.

A second motivation is that some of the buildings stop being useful very early on. Once you have a metal industry in place, there's no reason whatsoever to use the chipping table any longer. Similar thing with the carpentry workshop. With the building changes, and with upgrades, there will no longer be useless buildings.

[h1]More Details[/h1]
[h2]Buildings can be upgraded[/h2]
The upgrade system was introduced in the previous milestone with a limited scope - namely being able to improve the ship. This concept will be expanded in the next milestone, with the majority of buildings being able to support various upgrades to make them work better, unlock functionality, or give more bonuses. Craft buildings for instance can be upgraded to produce better quality items.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/7edd5d950ae80597ad98a897cfe8248525e32f16.jpg[/img]

Farms have also received an update, with upgrades effecting multiple fields, and certain crops requiring extra effort before they're unlocked. Also one of the upgrades unlocks a cat. Just thought I'd mention that.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/6a603cd11a06fdff21cf160ce4a3be0a094885e1.gif[/img]

[h2]Decorations[/h2]
The ability to decorate buildings has been a feature for quite a while, but the interface is rather complicated, and there aren't many items available to decorate with.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/1353f3e119ae2930bb2c1e14fd47eef134126c26.png[/img]

In the next milestone there will be many more items that can be used to decorate buildings, including carpets and items to hang up on walls. Additionally, some items can be recoloured, and the interface has been greatly simplified - as one can see from these two WIP videos:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tr7xmGKfIOM
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pdO0yJ_NqH4
[h2]Changes to Buildings[/h2]
Craft buildings will change to support a more horizontal view of what they're used for. 

Instead of having a Stoneworker and a Smithy for instance, there will be a toolworker workshop which exclusively creates tools (and upgrades), of various materials. This ties into the upgrade system, where unlocking certain materials will require the building to be upgraded. This should result in buildings which remain in use across the stages of the game.

Aside from buildings dedicated to crafting, other buildings will be added to tie in with the upgrade system - such as the farm (shown above), and the trader port.

[h2]Trade and Trade Goods[/h2]
Trade is set to become a bit more important. Tying into the decoration (and clothes) system, certain decorative items, exotic materials, or items used for high-level upgrades will not be available natively and will need to be purchased from a trader.

On the other hand - certain new craftable items will give more money when sold to traders, so you can more easily afford to get whatever you find useful. Traders will also be a bit more predictable in what goods they bring.

[h2]Clothing[/h2]
And lastly, there will be changes to the player's appearance. Instead of wearing armour all the time, the player will wear civilian clothing when in a safe area. The player should be able to choose this clothing - keeping in mind that certain outfits might need to be crafted, or traded for before they're unlocked.

[h1]Conclusions[/h1]
As always, this is all subject to change, depending on what works, and feedback. If you want to keep track of development, I have a weekly dev diary here

notes.title: Ironwood Update - Feature Roundup
notes.notes:
I'm pleased to announce that the Ironwood update is feature-done, and only needs some testing and balancing before it's released. No official date just yet, but hopefully in a week or two, depending on how it goes.

So let's take a quick look at what's coming with the next release...

[previewyoutube=TkoV33aTHTc;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]A summary of the changes[/h1]

- Materials are now unlocked by clearing a mine, or cutting a sapling from the forbidden forests. Also no more multi-ore rocks or multi-wood trees.
- Two boss enemies/arenas to fight in the mine
- A new type of map - the enchanted forest
- Ship upgrades, limited range and cloth
- Smarter enemies, ranged enemies, support enemies

And going into those in a bit more detail...

[h1]Material Unlocking[/h1]
With this next release, you no longer unlock materials (iron, orium, hardwood, heartwood) through capturing specific islands. Since they representing such important milestones, I felt that they deserved having something more interesting.

Let's start with metal. Now you start off with copper rocks on your starting island, and what appears to be an abandoned mine.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/8f5a9d56f8aa141209fc44069df9882811880ba7.png[/img]

Unlocking Iron, and Orium require you to defeat specific bosses. The first one is a giant spider which spawns more smaller spiders, whilst the second is an abandoned mining golem which can bring parts of the roof down on your head.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/187bd7fadd0b281c9cb736325cad486110771d8e.png[/img]

As you defeat those bosses, the mine becomes usable and you can get all the iron and orium you need from it.

As for wood - now there are special hardwood and heartwood bearing trees, which don't grow on your starting island... initially at least.

But there are enchanted forests available on the world map which have giant world-trees which you can grab a sapling off. If you do so, and survive a return to your ship, these special trees will start growing on your starting island, giving you a supply of these rare woods.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/88c66b922679be3575d7a7d0ff4c213d3b179963.png[/img]

Of course, the forests are not unguarded...

[h1]Ship upgrades[/h1]
The ship can now be upgraded. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/bdd3f2515f7dba0378d416f602729de98921249d.png[/img]

This feature brings with it two items of note. Firstly, the first column of upgrades is about extending the ship's range. It's designed in a way that you can't access the more dangerous islands until you unlock iron and hardwood, and the rest until you unlock orium and heartwood - making the progression a bit more clear.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/1d006ae19604019263ad138e5f9edccdf2c985db.png[/img]

Also, the speed upgrades require cloth. A new plant has been added which you can farm, then weave into cloth.

[h1]Enemies[/h1]
Enemies are now a bit smarter. Where applicable, they now move in a squad, so fighting them is not as easy as picking them off one at a time. 

Also a bit more variety has been added to enemies. The goblins, dark elves, and everpunished now have their own ranged and support enemy types. The ranged one just makes your life miserable until you get close enough to them to cut them down - having less defense than their peers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/b4ba825367d21ddec9c8943402e94b77f22ed60c.png[/img]

The support unit is different for each of the factions. The Everpunished one for instance, heals their peers - so they might be a priority when fighting them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/ebf0dc2d179288a9e300df1910ecfceb93fc13f9.jpg[/img]

So that's it in terms of major features. There are smaller features which I'll leave as a surprise to discover, and hopefully I'll have an official announcement in a week or two with the actual release.

And for reading this far, you get an image which you can use as a background.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/90edc35ef7f571684f0f598febda66205bc24ebb.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/494ddea85f0be3ae8884647dfce8ac720d605f56.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: Next Milestone Reveal - Ironwood
notes.notes:
With Alone released two weeks ago, it's time to look to the future, and see what's coming next.

[h1]Summary[/h1]

The next milestone is called [b]Ironwood[/b] and is planned to include the following main changes:

[list]
[*]Materials (hardwood, iron &c) will be unlocked by performing a special "mission"
[*]A mystical forest map defended by elves and dryads
[*]An abandoned mine infested with giant spiders
[*]Changes to enemies including better AI, ranged and AoE enemies
[*]Introduction of an upgrade system for the ship
[/list]
Bear in mind that everything here is subject to change, depending on what works, what doesn't, feedback received and that sort of thing.

[h1]Details and Motivation[/h1]
[h2]Materials Unlocking[/h2]
Unlocking different materials is a very important part of the game since using more primitive materials limits your effectiveness in resource collection and combat.

Currently you unlock a material by successfully claiming a specific island. The issue is that it's a similar process and fight to any other island you'd be attempting to claim, and so it lacks a clear sense of importance.

In this new milestone, this process will change. Metals will be unlocked by claiming and clearing an abandoned mine, and wood will be unlocked by taking a cutting off a World Tree in a new set of enchanted forest maps.

The enchanted forests are procedurally generated maps and are swarming with elves and dryads who will stop at nothing to prevent you reaching the World Tree and taking a sapling. If you succeed in this mission, then the appropriate trees will grow naturally in your start island, giving you access to the special wood.

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/1c1c481d253ed6c51f8104aeda5255f39d06944a.png[/img]

To aid you in your quest, there are a number of enchanted wells which will refresh your health - of course they're well defended.

The abandoned mine is still a work in progress and more information will be given in time.

[h2]Enemy Changes[/h2]
Aside from some specific boss enemies, most combat can easily be resolved by approaching the nearest enemy and hitting them until they stop moving.

This is going to change. Firstly, with the introduction of ranged enemies - such as the bowelf

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/7c253adb3a6cb2a2bd705e2cc401a02994eda1ac.png[/img]

As well as the addition of some "support" enemies which can make your life harder. The dryad for instance can cast an area of effect spell which will prevent you from moving - making you easy prey for her allies. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/9375d1d7610e655bf823e645a6ce1ad371a7adc3.png[/img]

The goblins and undead will also receive their own interesting units to make combat just a little bit trickier.

Of course, a lone bowelf is not much of a threat, which is why certain enemies can group up into squads - so they can support each other and require a bit more thought into how battle is approached.

[h2]Upgrade System[/h2]
The ability to Upgrade buildings is something that has been planned for a while now, and will be worked on fully in another milestone. However, as a first step, this milestone will include the ability to upgrade the ship to make travel times shorter, more comfortable, and perhaps even to make certain islands reachable.

[h1]In Conclusion[/h1]
I hope this has given a good overview of what to expect soon. There's no release date as of yet, since there's quite a bit of work to be done, but I will be giving frequent updates of features as they're implemented. Feedback is always welcome.

As always, if you want to keep track of weekly progress, you can follow the dev diaries here: https://devdiaries.alone.epicllama.games/

notes.title: Feature Focus - Islands
notes.notes:
After you've established yourself on your island, you might look across the sea and want to explore the rest of the world. In this Feature Focus, we can take a look at how you interact with the world outside of your island.

Fortunately you have a ship, although it will need repairs before it is seaworthy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/1ad47b5273d12e829667e7a6f4d3995cd75858ce.png[/img]

But once you've collected enough resources, and fixed the ship, you can use it to view the archipelago you find yourself in.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/867be13fe989bb987f43f955171d21249b8fcfbd.png[/img]

The world is procedurally generated each time, so the island position, types, resources, and names will be different in your playthrough.

However there are special islands, those marked with a resource icon, which are guaranteed to be generated, since they have special significance.

Each island will show different statistics on the right. Most importantly in the top corner describing just how dangerous the enemies you'll be facing. The resources below describe what the island looks like, and what resources you can gain from conquering the island.

And lastly, some islands will unlock access to special materials - such as iron or hardwood. Those are represented with an icon on the map, as well as the box on the right.

So, now you've chosen which island to visit, you can expect less than a warm welcome.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/93536c078c47c9a5b462c14a7ff36152771677b7.png[/img]

The islands are blighted, and armed and armoured goblins defend these mysterious towers. How dangerous these goblins are exactly will depend on the distance from your starting island, so there's a progression to it.

Once you succeed in defeating the goblins defending the tower, and using the gods-given power to purge the island of dark magic, you might think your quest is done.

But there's one last obstacle remaining between you and your conquest - the leader of the goblin tribes - the Shaman.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/6f3c90ca2758a5f807553c02af16cb099643e71d.png[/img]

The Shaman is not particularly strong in melee, but she has dark magics which will make you weaker, if they hit you. Also she's escorted by her bodyguards, which are more than happy to finish your off.

Having finally dispatched her - the island is now yours. But before you start to gain the benefits of your new conquest, you must secure it by repairing the fortress that lies on the island.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/dcda3b614ff6fac31876f50a6ec3412cb0e0fa05.png[/img]

And you've conquered your first island. Well done.

Now you can expand your Outpost through the Build menu. There are specific buildings which may be used to collect resources for you - and ship them over to your main island.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/88def95aef221119a1035db04ae010a89128111c.png[/img]

How many resources you'll earn depends on the quality of the resources on that island - so putting a woodcutter hut in a heavily forested island will get you much more.

Will you conquer the islands and bring them under your banner? Find out, in Alone.

notes.title: A look at Alone's Combat System
notes.notes:
The combat system has been reworked for the first major release. So let's take a quick look at the basics, special attacks, equipment, and how to defeat the various enemies that you'll encounter.

[previewyoutube=NRarn3hjI0s;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]The Philosophy[/h1]

Combat isn't the primary thing you'll be doing in Alone. You'll spend more time harvesting, crafting, or building up your settlement, but you will need to get your hands dirty once in a while. Either hunting to get access to important resources, or as part of the plan to rule over the surrounding islands.

The design philosophy behind the combat system is that it shouldn't be stressful, you shouldn't need to min-max a bunch of statistics to get an optimal build, and you shouldn't need to pore over walkthroughs and lists to determine the best equipment for a specific fight. 

Progressing through difficult combat should feel natural, if a specific area is difficult, the solution shouldn't be to grind unimportant areas until you get enough skill - but perhaps to make better equipment, or figure out better special attacks. 

[h1]Getting into it[/h1] 

Combat doesn't just happen anywhere. Your settlement is always a safe area, and you must visit a dangerous area in order to partake in combat. Options include the Cursed Crypts, where dangerous undead wander, the Forest - where you can get leather, meat, and furs from, or the Islands which are ruled by the Goblins.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/97ce4caf8007ec3bff9e70de3ef6109f50256b0d.png[/img]

[h1]The Basics[/h1]

When in a dangerous location, you automatically enter combat mode. The game controls change to allow you to carefully choose which direction you want to walk to using the mouse or cursor keys.

To attack an enemy, you simply click on them, and walk close enough so that you start hitting them, and they start hitting back.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/4fd51c9b2467576d8e3a798a4f72382b6a0d7d8b.png[/img]

When your enemy runs out of life, they die, and drop loot.

Just like your enemies, you have a limited amount of health, shown by the green circle, but also another blue circle - protection - which regenerates after a while. It won't regenerate to full though, only to as much health as you have.

Enemies have a level, which shows how dangerous they are in combat - and so do you.

The higher the level, the more powerful you are. Want to get to a higher level? Then defeat stronger enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/0f74448e5fba2cfc198b139d9211dafbe5618217.png[/img]

[h1]Equipment[/h1]

Of course, you can't fight empty handed. You do start off with a basic dagger, but if you want to do any serious fighting, you need the right equipment.

Depending on your choice of weapon, you can either fight in a balanced style, favour accuracy and critical hits, go for raw damage, or even eschew a shield for something two handed that packs a punch.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/d3927b5cf4ea36bf5058c4f704effafa646f085d.png[/img]

Similarly, you can choose heavy armour for some extra protection, or light armour to use special attacks more often.

Where do you get these nice pieces of equipment from ? You can find them as loot - although it's not going to be of particularly high quality - or you can make them yourself, which is the preferred option.

Good equipment requires rare materials to make, and especially good equipment requires especially rare materials to make.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/461262186f32bd63553d0fc7419efad4437513c2.png[/img]

Alternatively, you can wait until the appropriate trader comes along and see if she's got anything exotic for sale.

[h1]Special Attacks[/h1]

It wouldn't be a combat system without a whole slew of special attacks. Some attacks are attacks with a difference - such as more damage, or a chance to stun your opponent.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/8d4b9d19ed44a7ce4819d2b59a5c498a8f7439ea.gif[/img]

Other "attacks" will give you a boost to your abilities for a period of time - such as making you take less damage.

[previewyoutube=8QWK_y3xp-c;full][/previewyoutube]

Special attacks consume Rage. Rage is gained by defeating enemies, and that will charge up the Rage bar, up to a limit which is defined by the armour you're wearing. At higher rage levels, special attacks become more powerful and more effective.

Of course, you don't start off knowing all there is to know about special attacks. By defeating particularly dangerous boss enemies, you unlock new attacks, or higher levels for your existing attacks.

[h1]Losing[/h1]

Sometimes you fight enemies which are too powerful, and are defeated yourself. But don't worry, for it's not the end. Sure your equipment might take a beating, and you might feel pretty terrible for a while, but you'll be ready for round two in no time!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/adb280b2a01132d063d7a35b61b1e81affa9d235.png[/img]

So now you know what combat's all about, you are ready to brave the dangers, and overcome any obstacles you will come across, in Alone.
